oewn-01557242-a.learner: a word used with things you can count, most often after 'a', meaning a small number that is not stated exactly.
examples: Mr. Wickham, after a few moments, touched his hat
A few weeks, he believed.

oewn-00109247-r.learner: in this place, the place where the person speaking or writing is.
examples: Why, at that rate, you will have been here only six weeks.
Upon my word I say no more here than I might say in any house in the neighbourhood

oewn-00109415-r.learner: to this place, especially moving towards the person speaking.
examples: Come here, my love, I want to speak to you

oewn-00109541-r.learner: in this case, or about this particular point or detail.
examples: Here I must disagree with you, though I accept the rest of your argument.

oewn-00043413-r.learner: from that fact or reason, or as a result of it; used to bring in a conclusion that follows.
examples: it is very likely that he may fall in love with one of them, and therefore you must visit him as soon as he comes
You are too sensible a girl, Lizzy, to fall in love merely because you are warned against it; and, therefore, I am not afraid of speaking openly.

oewn-00295773-r.learner: as a result of what came before.
examples: They went to the library, therefore, and asked their father whether he would not wish them to make it known to her.
She was very equal, therefore, to address Mr. Bingley on the subject of the ball

oewn-00061477-r.learner: at an earlier time; in the past.
examples: the attention of every lady was soon caught by a young man, whom they had never seen before
what I was never bold enough to say before

oewn-00067181-r.learner: at the front, or in the front part.
examples: The banners went on before, and the crowd came slowly after.

oewn-01632781-v.learner: to make something happen as a result.
examples: in the case of the not very numerous authors who are the objects of the personal affection, it brings a curious consequence with it
the gaieties which that season generally brings

oewn-02081903-v.learner: to carry or lead something or someone with you to a place.
examples: I am glad I brought my bonnet, if it is only for the fun of having another band-box!
He brought it with him for us to see.

oewn-01441539-v.learner: to cause someone or something to reach a certain state or condition.
examples: a favourite with her mother, whose affection had brought her into public at an early age
Years of steady practice had brought her to a high level of skill.

oewn-02075880-a.learner: being the very one already spoken of, not another one.
examples: It was drawn at the same time as the other--about eight years ago.
Her prudent mother, occupied by the same ideas, forbore to invite him to sit by herself.

oewn-02070074-a.learner: very like another one in kind, quality, amount, or degree.
examples: The two sisters wore dresses of the same colour.

oewn-00356722-s.learner: still as it was, with its character or nature not changed.
examples: Many years passed, but the little village stayed the same.

oewn-01021652-v.learner: to tell someone something in a firm, certain and confident way.
examples: Mrs. Bennet assured her that they never sat there after dinner
And even Mary could assure her family that she had no disinclination for it.

oewn-00778313-v.learner: to tell someone that something is true so that they will feel sure of it.
examples: I am perfectly ready, I assure you, to keep my engagement
Only let me assure you, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that I can from my heart most cordially wish you equal felicity in marriage.

oewn-00892111-v.learner: to make something certain to be so.
examples: A large fortune assured her comfort for the rest of her life.

oewn-09489410-n.learner: everything that exists, anywhere at all.
examples: Philosophers still ask whether the world had a beginning.

oewn-08196607-n.learner: people in general, taken all together.
examples: It is, I believe, too little yielding; certainly too little for the convenience of the world.

oewn-07982551-n.learner: people in general, and especially a particular set of people who share an interest.
examples: Her singing made her well known in the world of music.

oewn-01545905-v.learner: to be resting with your upper body upright and your weight on your bottom.
examples: Elizabeth was sitting by herself the next morning, and writing to Jane

oewn-01988916-v.learner: to lower yourself into a seat.
examples: he had an opportunity of obliging her, in return, by sitting down to whist
On his quitting the room, she sat down, unable to support herself

oewn-02698724-v.learner: to stay somewhere, often with nothing particular to do.
examples: Mr. Bingley returned Mr. Bennet's visit, and sat about ten minutes with him in his library

oewn-10755748-n.learner: the brother of your father or your mother, or the husband of your aunt.
examples: I think I have heard you say that their uncle is an attorney in Meryton?
He is perfectly well-behaved, polite, and unassuming, said her uncle.

oewn-10755916-n.learner: someone you can turn to for help, advice and encouragement.
examples: The old teacher was an uncle to every new student who felt lost.

connotation.why: casts the helper in a warm, family-like light
